issues.description: The template's Stock.findStockIngredient method signature differs from the problem specification and the solution. The UML and solution define findStockIngredient(String): StockIngredient (single String parameter), but the template defines findStockIngredient(String, boolean). Moreover, other methods in the template (add and take) call findStockIngredient with a single String argument, causing a signature mismatch and compilation errors. This inconsistency will block students from implementing SealSaloon according to the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template Stock class to match the UML and solution by changing the method signature to public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) (remove the boolean parameter). Ensure add and take call this single-argument method. Alternatively, if the boolean flag is intended, update all internal calls (add/take) and the UML/spec to consistently use the two-parameter signature. Prefer making the template match the UML/solution (single-parameter) to avoid confusion.

issues.description: The Stock.findStockIngredient method is described in the problem statement and implemented in the solution as findStockIngredient(String), but the template repository exposes findStockIngredient(String, boolean caseSensitive). This signature mismatch (extra boolean parameter) breaks the direct mapping from the UML/problem text to the template and will confuse students implementing SealSaloon (they will expect a single-argument findStockIngredient). It may also cause compilation errors in starter code that calls findStockIngredient(String).
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template Stock API to match the problem and solution by providing public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name). Either remove the extra boolean parameter or add an overloaded single-argument findStockIngredient(String) that delegates to the existing implementation (e.g., defaulting case sensitivity), so student code and the UML map directly to the template.
